subject: MerchantX Onramp — success criteria & integration plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Murphy <alex@merchantx.com>, Lucy Chen <lucy@merchantx.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MerchantX call follow-up — draft acceptance criteria and handoff

Alex / Lucy — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have a single source of truth. I tried to keep this focused on the POC acceptance criteria, timeline, and dev handoff items we discussed.

Summary of ask from MerchantX:
- Real-time chat suggestion feature (low-latency completions for suggestions) for web checkout flow.
- Streaming responses to surface suggestions as the agent types.
- Integration with MerchantX tool calling layer to execute product lookups for out-of-stock suggestions.

Proposed POC success criteria (draft):
1) Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end suggestion latency <= 180ms for 1–2 token prefix on US region.
2) Quality: Precision@3 for suggestions >= 78% on MerchantX curated prompt set (sample attached).
3) Reliability: No more than 0.5% error rate (HTTP 5xx / timeouts) during 72-hour ramp.
4) Integration: Working tool-call flow where Redwood returns a structured tool call (JSON) and MerchantX executes product lookup and returns results within 250ms.

POC scope and timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): Finalize success criteria and sign off on required sample prompts / evaluation dataset.
- Week 1: Dev handoff — Redwood provides SDK examples, streaming guide, and a small sandbox endpoint.
- Week 2: MerchantX implements SDK integration and tool-calling glue; run smoke tests.
- Week 3: Ramp load to validate latency and error rates; collect quality metrics.
- Week 4: Acceptance window and retrospective.

Ownership suggestions:
- Redwood dev lead (Ben) — SDK examples, streaming sample, assist tool-calling wiring.
- Redwood technical PD (Sofia) — SLA targets, observability hooks, instrumentation checklist.
- MerchantX eng (Alex) — implement SDK, map tool calling, run evaluation.

Attachments: merchantx_poc_scope.xlsx (sample prompts + success criteria table); redwood_sdk_onramp_checklist.md (SDK steps and routes).

Open questions for alignment:
- Does MerchantX need a dedicated token budget for the POC or will initial traffic fit our shared sandbox?
- Are there any corporate firewall / CORS restrictions that would prevent streaming over SSE from your frontend?

Next steps: Please reply with signoff on the success criteria (or edits) and confirm a dev kickoff time (I propose Wed 12/02 10am PT).

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0182
From: Alex Murphy <alex@merchantx.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lucy Chen <lucy@merchantx.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MerchantX call follow-up — draft acceptance criteria and handoff

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear summary. A few quick notes / clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency target — 180ms P95 is ambitious but aligns with our UX goals. We have a fallback to local heuristics at >250ms, so the POC should show we can meet the threshold on average under our sandbox traffic.

2) Quality — Lucy will pull a 500-prompt sample from our historical suggestions dataset and share it by EOD tomorrow. We may ask to tweak Precision@3 to Precision@5 depending on how the prompt set behaves.

3) Tool calling — we absolutely need structured tool calls (not just text hints). Our product lookup API accepts a JSON query payload and returns results; the 250ms target is achievable if Redwood returns structured calls quickly.

4) Security / network: MerchantX frontend is behind a stricter CSP, but we can open connections to Redwood streaming endpoints. We will list the allowed origins and IP ranges in a follow-up.

5) Token budget: for the POC traffic we expect low volume (~5k tokens/day). If you need a dedicated sandbox quota, please advise.

We can do the dev kickoff on Wed 12/02 10am PT — that works for Alex, Lucy, and I. Please send the calendar invite.

— Alex
Alex Murphy
VP Engineering, MerchantX
alex@merchantx.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Murphy <alex@merchantx.com>, Lucy Chen <lucy@merchantx.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MerchantX call follow-up — draft acceptance criteria and handoff

Great — thanks Alex, excited to get started. Two items I wanted to call out pre-kickoff so our engineers can pack the right artifacts into the calendar invite: 

Technical artifacts Redwood will provide at kickoff:
- SDK quickstart repo (node + python) with examples showing: connect(), stream(), and on_tool_call(callback) patterns.
- API route reference for the POC endpoints: POST /v1/generate (batch), POST /v1/stream (SSE), POST /v1/tool_call (structured tool payload).
- Streaming behavior doc: chunking, partial tokens, reconnect semantics, SSE heartbeats.
- Example tool-calling contract (JSON schema) and an end-to-end sample where Redwood suggests a product and returns {"tool_call": {"name":"product_lookup","args":{...}}}.

Integration notes for MerchantX devs:
- Use the SDK sample that wires stream() on the frontend to receive partial suggestions and show the top suggestion as typing occurs.
- Implement a thin proxy that converts Redwood tool_call JSON to your internal product lookup API (so we don't need backend token exchange on first pass).
- Instrument the SDK with our telemetry hooks (request_id, route, latency_ms) so Sofia can pull P95 latency from the console during ramp.

Pre-kickoff deliverable requests for MerchantX:
- Sample prompt set (Lucy) — please upload to the Drive link.
- Allowlist of origins / IPs (Alex) — to verify streaming connectivity.
- Test product lookup API endpoint (staging) and sample credentials for proxy (will be used only during the POC).

I've attached the starter checklist: redwood_sdk_onramp_checklist.md and updated the merchantx_poc_scope.xlsx to include fields for telemetry keys.

I'll send the calendar invite for Wed 12/02 10am PT and include a 45-minute tech sync + 15-minute follow-up slot for Biz/CS.

Best,

Ben
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Murphy <alex@merchantx.com>, Lucy Chen <lucy@merchantx.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MerchantX call follow-up — draft acceptance criteria and handoff

Looping in a quick instrumentation checklist and who will own what on our side so we have no ambiguity after signoff.

Redwood POC instrumentation & SLO checklist (Neha) — items we will validate during ramp:
- Request tracing: ensure request_id surfaces in SDK logs and console (owner: Ben).
- Token accounting: token_count per request in telemetry (owner: Ben).
- Streaming reliability: reconnect events, SSE drop counts (owner: Sofia).
- Tool-call latency histogram: measure from Redwood outbound to MerchantX staging response (owner: Sofia).
- Quality eval harness: automated Precision@k scripts against MerchantX sample prompts (owner: Neha).

Acceptance gating rules (finalized):
- Gate 1 (Instrumentation): All telemetry keys present and visible in Redwood Console.
- Gate 2 (Performance): Latency P95 <= 180ms on Redwood Console over a 72-hour continuous ramp.
- Gate 3 (Quality): Precision@3 >= 78% on the agreed dataset for the acceptance window.
- Gate 4 (Tooling): Successful structured tool-calls for 98% of lookups during the acceptance window.

If MerchantX signs off on these, we'll move the kickoff invite to confirmed and start the sandbox quota provisioning.

Action items for MerchantX before kickoff:
- Upload sample prompts to the Drive link.
- Provide staging product_lookup endpoint + creds (temp).
- Send allowlist entries for streaming origin/IPs.

I will prepare the evaluation harness and share run instructions in the Drive folder by Monday morning.

-Neha
Principal Product Manager | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
